rows.contract: Executable hook source parses before it is used.
rows.disposition: retire the two Bash hook syntax checks; retain canonical shim syntax and execute native version/pre/post
rows.reason: The native hook has no Bash body to parse. Rust compilation and the actual core calls cover the replacement.

rows.contract: The self budget ceiling is below the registered runtime timeout.
rows.disposition: core-smoke.sh core_smoke_budget calls native budget-config and reads the installer timeout

rows.contract: A rewritten no-id command finds the pre hook's pending record.
rows.disposition: core-smoke.sh core_smoke_pending executes native pre and post for all eight commands and checks record consumption

rows.contract: Views, payload reconstruction and grammar are read from the shipped reader.
rows.disposition: core-reader.sh calls lex, grammar and reader; existing fixed and measured expectations remain

rows.contract: An apostrophe inside a single-quoted awk program must not execute shell code.
rows.reason: The Rust lexer is compiled code, not a Bash string evaluated as awk. Quoted input and byte-preservation expectations remain in scan-contract.

rows.contract: The driver owns the shell reading; callers cannot silently switch readings.
rows.disposition: core/reader_tests.rs tests missing reading, explicit reading/view separation, and driver cleanup
rows.reason: Bash call-site and global-assignment greps have no native target.

rows.contract: Invalid payload units fail explicitly; recursive scripts reach substitutions without silently ending the reader.
rows.disposition: core/reader_tests.rs preserves all twelve unit cases, deep recursion and failure propagation
rows.reason: Rust has no set -e subshell return-status hazard; the Bash setE_script control is retired.

rows.contract: Statement cuts and words respect reading-specific redirections, comments and heredocs.
rows.disposition: reader statements supplies the production result to the unchanged fixed expectations and event contract

rows.contract: Manager and shell sets agree with the pipe recognizer, including case and boundaries.
rows.disposition: core/reader_tests.rs tests the production grammar and pipe predicate on the original name lists

rows.contract: One text, view or reading must not reuse another's cached bytes or lose DIVERGE.
rows.disposition: core/reader_tests.rs reuses one Run across texts, views and readings and checks DIVERGE
rows.reason: Native Run has no checksum-keyed disk memo. Planting cksum files and requiring PLANTED to be returned is retired, not counted as native cache coverage.

rows.contract: Scanner failure is distinguishable from no-match and reaches UNDECIDED settlement.
rows.disposition: core/reader_tests.rs checks invalid view/reading propagation; pre/reader_tests.rs calls the production settlement with failure and working controls; core-reader-check.py settlement exercises public pre with unclosed install and non-install input
rows.reason: The native reader starts no awk/grep/sed processes. Their call-index failures and grep flag-file failures are retired. No injected subprocess failure is claimed.

rows.contract: Reader inputs and offsets belong to original command or executable payload bytes.
rows.disposition: core-reader-check.py source-map checks native payload shape and every source byte against the original command, including nested child fixtures
rows.reason: The awk-call trace is retired. Source-map checks cover payload attribution, not an inventory of every native lex call.

rows.contract: Spec and statement read failures cannot become empty successful readings.
rows.disposition: core/reader_tests.rs checks missing-reading pieces and invalid-view failure propagation through facts; pre/reader_tests.rs checks final settlement
rows.reason: Bash function-body bans on sed/tr/awk/grep and failing awk executables no longer target the native reader.

rows.contract: The failure discriminator names census managers, ignores case, and needs no scanner subprocess.
rows.disposition: pre/reader_tests.rs calls the exact discriminator on the census and fixed controls, and checks its connection to settlement

rows.contract: Batched grep answers and ecosystem selection equal individual grep calls despite multiline and invalid-byte input.
rows.disposition: retire batch/single equivalence; retain four corpora and seeded generator in the native facts battery, and ten fixed ecosystem expectations in both public and unit tests
rows.reason: Rust has no Bash grep batching or line-number map. The historical comparison count and failgrep controls are not native evidence.

rows.contract: Command-specific options are selected correctly; table entries are unique and reachable.
rows.disposition: core grammar table checks plus direct native option_class and command tests
rows.reason: The mutable synthetic zz table is retired because the native table is a compiled constant. The concrete bun x -p regression and all actual table lookups remain tested.

rows.source: smoke.sh CLI ledger source rows and fixtures
rows.contract: The CLI ledger writer, validation and approval fixtures still use the Bash library.
rows.disposition: preserve; these rows still exercise shipped CLI code and are not counted as native reader coverage

rows.contract: Compaction keeps evidence bytes, archives INFO, bounds retained generations, honors the rotation lock and derives advisory.log from the state directory.
rows.disposition: preserve all seven CLI Bash rows; add core-advisory-retention.py with real pre/post log growth, disk and gzip readback, exact generation membership, and state-path assertions
